slides.title: WHAT A 95% CONFIDENCE INTERVAL REALLY MEANS
THE SETUP
slides.note: The 95% describes the method, not one interval: it captures the true value in about 95% of repeated samples.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: A sample gives x̄ = 50 with margin of error 4. Find the 95% interval.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: How do you interpret (46, 54) at 95% confidence?
steps: Say: we are 95% confident the true mean is between 46 and 54
The true mean is a fixed number, not random

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: There is a 95% probability the true mean is in (46, 54)
points: Once computed, the interval either contains the true mean or it doesn't.
A larger sample or lower confidence level gives a narrower interval.

pageTitle: Confidence Intervals: What They Really Mean
description: Learn how to build and correctly interpret a confidence interval with two worked examples.
